CONFIRM C0021 | `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., stderr="TIMEOUT")` on timeout, but `run_pyright()/run_ruff()/run_bandit()/run_mypy()` only special-case `"NOT_FOUND"`. On timeout they proceed into parse logic, usually yielding `[]`, which makes timeout indistinguishable from healthy no-findings. This also feeds the false-availability bug in `scan_health()`.

CONFIRM C0001 | In `scan_health()`, `tools_available[tool_name] = True` is set whenever the runner returns without raising. But each runner returns `[]` for missing binaries (`stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`), so missing tools are reported as available. This misleads the insect brain’s health signal.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually test fixes in a sandboxed project context. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it copies only the single target file to a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file. For imports and cross-file references, the patched file is no longer evaluated in the same package/module context as the real source tree. Evidence: the code never copies sibling modules, package structure, configs, or test files into `tmpdir`; post-fix tool runs target only `patched_path`.
FOLLOW: This can silently misclassify harmful fixes as SAFE/NEUTRAL or safe fixes as harmful. A change that breaks imports, package-relative references, or inter-module contracts with `immune_agents.py` / `insect_brain.py` may not be detected because those dependencies are absent from the sandbox. Since immune stage 4 uses `evaluate_fixes()` to mark findings `verified=True` when verdict is SAFE or NEUTRAL, a false SAFE here can close bugs prematurely and activate NK “bug closed” suppression on later rounds. That is a high-impact wrong-result path, not just a quality issue.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create the sandbox as a copy of the relevant source tree (at minimum the common parent directory of `source_paths`), patch the target file at its relative path inside that copied tree, and run pyright/ruff/bandit/tests from that sandbox root against the sandboxed relative file/project. Do not evaluate the patched file in isolation.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — optional test execution in `evaluate_fix()` is not sandbox-safe and often does not test the patched code. The function writes the patched file into `tmpdir` but then runs the caller-provided `test_cmd` unchanged with only `cwd=tmpdir`. In context, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` calls this with `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. From inside `tmpdir`, that path usually does not exist, and even if tests are discovered via absolute/import paths they will import the real project tree, not the patched temp file. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` never rewrites test paths, never sets `PYTHONPATH`, and never mirrors the repo into the tempdir.
FOLLOW: The “tests_passed” signal can become a false positive or false negative. False positive: tests execute against real source and pass, so a harmful patch is marked SAFE/NEUTRAL. False negative: pytest cannot find `bench/tests/` under `tmpdir`, so otherwise safe fixes are marked HARMFUL. Downstream, fix verification in the immune pipeline depends on this verdict to set `verified=True`; wrong test targeting corrupts closure/escalation decisions across rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when `test_cmd` is provided, run tests against the sandboxed project root: copy the needed project subtree into `tmpdir`, patch in place there, and rewrite relative test paths in `test_cmd` to the sandbox copy before execution.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can label a fix SAFE even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as another tool’s count decreases more. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues` and returns HARMFUL only if `total_net > 0`. Example from the implemented logic: `+3` bandit issues and `-5` ruff issues yields `total_net = -2`, so verdict becomes SAFE. That violates the documented rule “SAFE: no new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: This is a silent wrong-result bug in the key fix-evaluation capability. Security regressions or new type errors can be masked by unrelated lint reductions, causing harmful fixes to be marked SAFE and then `verified=True` in the immune pipeline. That can wrongly close findings and suppress rediscovery.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify HARMFUL if any of `net_type_errors > 0`, `net_ruff_errors > 0`, or `net_bandit_issues > 0`; only use aggregate reduction to decide SAFE after confirming no category regressed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring matching unrelated path fragments from free text. Evidence: it extracts any `[\w/\\]+\.py` token from `finding.description + " " + finding.proposed_fix`, then returns the first `source_path` where `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. The `match in sp_path` branch is overly loose; a basename or partial path embedded in prose can match multiple files, and the function returns the first one.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation may patch and score the wrong file while reporting a verdict for the finding’s ID. That produces silently wrong SAFE/HARMFUL judgments and can also make the “no source modification” sandbox appear to work while evaluating an unrelated file. Since immune stage 4 trusts this result for verification, wrong file resolution can close or reject the wrong bug.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict matching to exact normalized path equality or basename equality when unique among `source_paths`; if resolution is ambiguous, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of guessing.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0005 | The “fix evaluation is sandboxed” feature is also partially dead/misleading in a more serious way than missing categories: the implementation only sandboxes a lone file, not the project context, and test execution is not rewritten to hit the sandbox. The feature fires, but not against the patched codebase the interface promises. This is a functional gap, not just documentation drift.
